title: Grateful Dead Live at Felt Forum - Madison Square Garden on 1971-12-05

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear FM broadcast of a high‑energy 1971 show with smoking Truckin', Bertha and Comes A Time, despite some early static.
ai_review.review: The recording captures an exhilarating late‑'71 performance that many fans cite as a career peak – standout renditions of Truckin', Bertha, Sugar Magnolia, Tennessee Jed and a soaring Comes A Time.  The FM source is remarkably crisp compared to tape bootlegs, though listeners note a faint static hiss at the start and a weaker mix on Phil’s solo in Bertha.  Overall the musical firepower and vocal brilliance outweigh the minor technical quirks.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently five‑star praise for the show’s performance and only mild, uniform comments about static; recording quality is good enough to enhance a superb concert.

recording_quality.technical_notes: FM broadcast source is notably crisp and clear, far superior to older tape copies.  Some reviewers mention a faint static hiss at the beginning and a weaker mix on Phil's Bertha solo.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set rides a tight wave of high‑energy first‑set classics that transition smoothly into a fiery second set, highlighted by an explosive Truckin' and a heartfelt Comes A Time.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for his vocal phrasing on Comes A Time and overall tone throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Phil: Highlighted for his storytelling bass solo in Bertha, with some reviewers noting a weak mix early on.
band_member_comments.Bob: Vocals on Jack Straw, Tennessee Jed and other first‑set numbers singled out as especially strong.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s powerful voice and keyboard work receive glowing remarks; Keith is noted as part of the great blues backing.
